descs.t: Bardella has been reelected president of France's National Rally, Bloomberg reports, as riots and protests spread across France. Police have charged crowds in several cities, and more than 200 people have been handed swift sentences, according to posts from the scene. We walk through the vote, the clashes and what the street violence means for France's right.

Bardella was reelected to lead the National Rally while counter-protesters gathered at its congress and riots spread through French cities. A far-left LFI lawmaker was filmed taking pictures with masked rioters waving Palestinian flags. We break down how the unrest shapes Bardella's case and the pressure it puts on Macron.

France's streets are burning, and Bardella has just been handed another term leading the National Rally. In one video a neighbour begs rioters to stop a fire because children are inside, and they refuse. We look at what the videos show, how the police answered, and why the right says it warned about this.

intro.plain: Big news out of France. Bardella has been reelected president of the National Rally, and it happened while riots spread through French cities, with police charging crowds and more than 200 people already sentenced, according to reports. That puts the far-right leader at the center of the biggest argument in France right now. So tell me in the chat: does this unrest make Bardella stronger?
intro.mid: France is in the streets, and the National Rally just gave Bardella another term as its president. Counter-protesters gathered at the congress, riots hit Lille, Nice and Montpellier, and a far-left lawmaker was filmed posing with masked rioters. The right says this is exactly what it warned about. Chat, I want your read: who gains from these riots, Bardella or Macron?
intro.bold: Look at France right now. Fires set against buildings with kids inside, a police officer seriously injured by a brick in Lille, and a far-left lawmaker posing for pictures with masked rioters. And in the middle of it, Bardella has been reelected to lead the National Rally. Chat, tell me straight: should French police have cracked down sooner?

hook.plain: Bardella has been reelected to lead France's National Rally, just as riots spread across French cities. Here is what the vote means and what the streets are telling us.
hook.mid: More than 200 rioters sentenced, police charging crowds, and the National Rally keeps Bardella at the top. Here is what France's unrest means for its right.
hook.bold: A woman begs rioters to stop. There are kids in that building. They refuse. Now Bardella has another term, and France has to decide who keeps order.

descs.t: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield are back to their old speeds, while Elon Musk says Kyiv violated Starlink's terms by using the civilian service for offensive drone strikes, Reuters reports. Zelenskyy thanked Trump and the State Department for restoring service. We walk through what each side says and what separates Starlink from Starshield.

Elon Musk says Ukraine broke Starlink's rules by using the civilian network for offensive drone strikes, even as Zelenskyy announced that Starlink and Starshield speeds were restored. Ukrainian voices call Musk's account false, and critics in the US want Congress to look. We break down the claims and what this fight means for Ukraine's drone war.

Ukraine's battlefield internet runs through one company, and Elon Musk now says Kyiv broke the rules by using civilian Starlink to strike with drones. Zelenskyy says speeds are back to normal and thanked Trump. We look at who is telling the truth, what Starshield is, and how much power one man holds over this war.

intro.plain: Starlink is back to normal in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says, with Starlink and Starshield restored to the speeds they had before the restrictions. But Elon Musk now says Kyiv violated Starlink's terms by using the civilian service for offensive drone strikes. Ukrainian voices say that is false. Chat, tell me: should a private company decide how a country at war uses its network?
intro.mid: Here is the fight of the day. Zelenskyy thanked Trump and the State Department for getting Starlink and Starshield back to full speed in Ukraine. Hours later Elon Musk said Kyiv broke Starlink's terms by using the civilian service for drone strikes, and Starshield is the military version. Chat, what do you think: is Musk right, or is this spin?
intro.bold: One man's network is running a war. Elon Musk says Ukraine used civilian Starlink to kill people with offensive drone strikes and broke his terms. Zelenskyy says the speeds are back and thanked Trump. Ukrainian voices call Musk a liar. Somebody here is not telling the truth. Chat, who do you believe, Musk or Kyiv?

hook.plain: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield are back to full speed. Elon Musk says Kyiv broke the rules to get there. Here is what each side claims.
hook.mid: Zelenskyy thanked Trump for restoring Starlink. Then Musk said Ukraine had violated its terms with drone strikes. Here is where the civilian network ends and Starshield begins.
hook.bold: Elon Musk just accused Ukraine of using his civilian satellites to strike with drones. Kyiv says that is false. Here is who is right, and why it matters for this war.

descs.t: Huge crowds filled the streets of Paris as protests over soaring living costs spread across France, and Sky News reports troops were sent into the city. Police used tear gas and water cannons as parts of the march turned into clashes, Fox News and ABC News report. We walk through the aerial footage, the clashes and what the protesters are demanding.

Paris saw a massive turnout as protests swept France, with aerial footage showing a sea of demonstrators from Porte d'Italie. Riot police charged into crowds, fired tear gas and turned water cannons on protesters, and troops were sent into the city. We break down what started as a march, how it became a confrontation, and the pressure on Macron.

Paris is in chaos. Rioters threw Molotov cocktails at police, according to posts from the scene, and one woman showed how a fire started on the street destroyed her apartment. Police answered with tear gas, water cannons and charges into the crowd. We look at the footage street by street and what it says about where France is heading.

intro.plain: Paris is packed with protesters right now. Aerial footage shows a sea of demonstrators, the protests are over soaring living costs, and Sky News reports troops have been sent into the city. Police have used tear gas and water cannons as parts of the march turned into clashes. Chat, I want to hear from you: is this a protest about money, or about something bigger?
intro.mid: Let's go straight to Paris. A massive turnout, protests across France over the cost of living, troops sent into the city, and riot police charging into crowds with tear gas and water cannons. Some of this started peaceful and did not stay that way. Chat, here is my question: did the police lose control, or did they finally take it?
intro.bold: Look at Paris right now. Molotov cocktails thrown at police, according to people on the ground, water cannons in the streets, and a woman whose apartment burned after rioters lit a fire below it. Troops have been sent into the city. This is France today. Chat, tell me honestly: how much worse does it get before Macron changes course?

hook.plain: A sea of demonstrators stretched across Paris, and troops were sent into the city. Here is what the protests are about and how they turned into clashes.
hook.mid: Tear gas, water cannons and riot police charging into the crowd. Paris went from a march to a confrontation, and here is how it happened.
hook.bold: Rioters lit a fire on the street, and a woman's apartment above it burned. That is Paris right now. Here is what the footage shows, street by street.

Lisa's Press Play opened with 8.31 million Spotify streams across six songs, second only to Alter Ego among her own debuts and ahead of LALISA. SaWaDiKa climbed 123 spots to number 71 on the Global Spotify chart. We break down where the debut ranks and which tracks are climbing.

Lisa just posted the biggest K-pop solo album debut of 2026 on Spotify, with Press Play hitting 8,312,603 streams on day one and topping the Worldwide iTunes Album chart for a second day. We look at the numbers, the rivals and what this week means for her solo career.

descs.t: Barack Obama says Iran did not have nuclear weapons because of the deal he put in place, and blames the current Iran war on Trump pulling out of it. Netanyahu says Iran has restarted its nuclear program, and Trump says he may have to finish the job with Iran or make a deal. We walk through each claim and what the record shows.

Obama argues diplomacy kept Iran from a nuclear weapon without firing a missile, while Netanyahu warns Iran has restarted its program and intends to destroy Israel. Iran's president Pezeshkian blames the US for a failed interim peace deal, and Iran threatens a global internet blackout if America restarts the war. We break down who is right and what comes next.

Obama is back defending the Iran deal, saying it stopped the regime from getting nuclear weapons. Netanyahu says Tehran has restarted its nuclear program and plans to destroy Israel. We look at why the regime keeps coming back to the table, what Obama's deal gave it, and why pressure is the only language Tehran respects.

intro.plain: Barack Obama is talking about Iran. He says Iran did not have nuclear weapons because of his deal, and he did not have to fire a missile to do it. At the same time Netanyahu says Iran has restarted its nuclear program, and Trump says he may have to finish the job or make a deal. Chat, who do you think has this right?
intro.mid: Obama is defending his Iran deal again, saying diplomacy kept Iran from nukes and blaming this war on the deal being torn up. Netanyahu says Tehran has restarted its program. Iran is threatening a global internet blackout if America restarts the war, and Pezeshkian says Iran still wants an agreement. Chat, my question: would another deal stop the regime, or buy it time?
intro.bold: Obama says his deal kept Iran from nuclear weapons. Netanyahu says the regime has restarted its program and plans to destroy Israel. And the regime is threatening to black out the global internet if America hits it again. I lived under this regime, and I know what it does with time and money. Chat, tell me straight: deal, or finish the job?

hook.plain: Obama says Iran had no nuclear weapons because of his deal. Netanyahu says Iran has restarted its program. Here is what each one is claiming.
hook.mid: Obama blames this Iran war on the deal Trump pulled out of. Trump says he may finish the job or make a deal. Here is what is really on the table.
hook.bold: Obama says he stopped Iran's bomb without firing a missile. Netanyahu says the regime has restarted. Here is why his story does not hold.

descs.t: Multiple voters in Bexar County, Texas, report touchscreen voting machines switching their selections from Democrat Gina Hinojosa to the Republican candidate. Texas early voting is close to 3 million votes, according to posts tracking turnout. We walk through the reports, the turnout numbers and the races for Talarico and Hinojosa.

Voters in Bexar County say touchscreen machines flipped their Hinojosa votes, while James Talarico tells supporters Democrats will take back Texas. Republican voices warn Democrats are outvoting them in Tarrant County. We break down what is confirmed, what is claimed, and what the early vote says about Texas.

Texas voters say machines changed their votes, Democrats are drawing huge lines in San Antonio, and Republicans are warning of a five alarm turnout problem. We look at the Bexar County reports, the early vote numbers and whether Texas is really in play this time.

intro.plain: Let's talk about Texas. Multiple voters in Bexar County report touchscreen machines switching their picks from Democrat Gina Hinojosa to the Republican. Early voting there is close to 3 million, and James Talarico is campaigning hard on college campuses. Chat, if you are voting in Texas, tell me: did you check your ballot screen before you hit cast?

Voters in Bexar County say touchscreen machines flipped their Hinojosa votes, Talarico says Democrats will shock the nation and take back Texas, and Republicans warn they are being outvoted in Tarrant County. That is the report out of Bexar County, and it lands while Democrats draw enormous lines in San Antonio and Republicans call their own turnout a five alarm warning. This race is closer than anyone expected. Chat, tell me straight: does Texas stay red?
